title: KRR: Efficient and Scalable Kernel Record Replay
problem: Kernel record-replay systems incur significant recording overhead and struggle to scale deterministically across multi-core systems. Efficiently capturing kernel events while enabling fast, correct replay across many processors remains a fundamental challenge.
motivation: Efficient and scalable kernel record-replay enables developers to debug, test, and analyze complex system behaviors in production-like multi-core environments.
method: KRR uses selective event logging to minimize recording overhead, optimized storage and compression of trace data, and parallel deterministic replay mechanisms. The system likely leverages kernel instrumentation hooks and efficient data structures to scale recording and replay across many cores while preserving execution determinism.
key_novelty: First system to achieve both low recording overhead and efficient scaling to many-core systems simultaneously in kernel record-replay.
contributions: Efficient low-overhead kernel event recording mechanism
Scalable deterministic replay across multi-core systems
Optimized trace compression and storage strategy
Comprehensive evaluation demonstrating efficiency and scalability gains
limitations: Limitations not discussed from title-only analysis.
primary_theme: Efficient deterministic record-replay for kernel debugging
